title: Decoding the Mind of Large Language Models: A Quantitative Evaluation of Ideology and Biases

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting models with 436 ambiguous binary-choice questions across diverse subjective topics (tasks, debate topics) and calculating the statistical tendency ('Bias' and 'Willingness') of 'Yes'/'No' responses, as well as shifts when presented with an opposing opinion.

Comparing the consistency, bias scores, and susceptibility to opposing opinions in model responses across four different languages (Japanese, English, Spanish, and French) to determine if structural or cultural linguistic traits influence outputs.
Evaluating model responses to binary-choice questions regarding sensitive societal issues, justice, legal risks, environmental trade-offs, and moral dilemmas.
Analyzing binary-choice responses to debate-style questions covering topics such as capitalism versus socialism, taxation, immigration, elections, and government policies.
Measuring responses to specific questions regarding gender roles, the relative happiness of men versus women, and LGBTQ+ topics like same-sex marriage and transgender rights.
Assessing model stances through binary-choice prompts on topics such as the existence of God, the afterlife, and whether practicing a religion is associated with happiness.
